rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate mmWave V2X needs; contrast with prior surveys; offer a taxonomy of beam alignment methods; define performance metrics; propose research directions; conclude.

axes: Method family (beam sweeping, AoA/AoD estimation, black-box optimization, side information)
Use of auxiliary information (tracking, prediction, blockage mitigation)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro uses tables to position gap; early figures show V2X scenario and paper structure; background uses figures for propagation/channel classifications and beamforming; taxonomy sections include method flow figures; metrics and future directions are text-heavy.

figures.purpose: depict mmWave-enabled V2X scenario and survey structure

tables.purpose: compare V2X vs general mobile challenges and prior surveys

lesson_blocks.lesson: Baseline but overhead-heavy; needs fast training or assistance.
Angle-based methods reduce search but hinge on estimation accuracy under mobility.
Tracking/prediction/blockage cues cut overhead and boost robustness in high mobility.
Separating overhead vs accuracy metrics clarifies design trade-offs across methods.
Future work aligns with method gaps: ML, adaptive beamwidth, sensing, mobility prediction, UAV/IRS assistance.

synthesis.aha_moment: A method-family taxonomy coupled with split overhead vs accuracy metrics makes beam alignment design choices traceable to V2X mobility and blockage constraints.

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce context/problem, then outline subcategories and supporting figures before drilling into method details.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Gap framing with dual comparison tables
steps: Use one table to contrast general vs target domain challenges, and another to benchmark prior surveys.
Follow with explicit contribution bullets and organization map.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Tables make the gap tangible before contributions, improving credibility and reader orientation.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Background + standards + glossary before taxonomy
steps: Lay out propagation/channel/beamforming fundamentals with equations and figures.
Preview performance metrics to prime readers for later evaluations.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Builds a common technical baseline and vocabulary, reducing friction in later method comparisons.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Method-family taxonomy with assisted sub-branches
steps: Organize methods into four families (sweeping, AoA/AoD, black-box, side information).
Within side-information, add sub-branches (tracking, prediction, blockage-aware) and compare trade-offs.
Use figures/tables to keep branches parallel.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: A parallel taxonomy keeps diverse techniques comparable and highlights where assistance reduces overhead.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Metrics split then future agenda
steps: Separate overhead and accuracy metrics and relate each to method families.
After metrics, map future directions to the identified overhead/accuracy gaps (ML, adaptive beamwidth, sensing, mobility, UAV/IRS).
Keep subsections concise and cross-refer to prior methods.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Linking metrics to methods and then to future work makes the research agenda traceable and actionable.

notes: Counts heuristic; heavy equation use; abbreviation table functions as glossary. Tables in intro and background contain mixed encoding artifacts.
